From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap + Next Tests: multi-region latency run / Redwood vs hyperscalers

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the Acme OGX team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary goal: 95th/99th p95 latency stability for inference across EU and US regions under synthetic peak load (50 rps per model).
- Important metrics: cold-start p95, steady-state token p95, tail latency (99th), and regional throughput.
- Data residency: any logs/metrics for EU tests must stay in eu-central-1 and be accessible via your audit token.
- Competitive context: you're testing Redwood against Hyperscaler X managed endpoint and Vendor Y API. You care about predictable SLOs and fallback behavior.

Proposed concrete next tests (week of 16 Feb):
1) EU Gateway run (primary): 3 x 10-minute windows at 10/25/50 rps — compare Redwood hosted EU node vs Hyperscaler X EU endpoint. Collect p50/p95/p99 and cold-start samples.
2) US burst run: single 30-minute test to validate autoscale handoff and incremental latency.
3) Controlled cold-start: 20 sequential short-lived containers to measure cold-start distribution (your ask).

Action items (owners & timeline):
- Marcus (me): provide test harness CSV and sample requests by EOD today. [Attachment: redwood-v-hyperscalers-latency-sample.csv]
- Soojin: coordinate dedicated EU node config and ensure logs are stored in eu region (due Mon 16 Feb).
- Marissa: share canary rollout policy template and suggested traffic split for A/B.
- John / Jane (Acme): share a point-of-contact and test credentials for your staging endpoints; confirm availability Mon 16 Feb 09:00 CET.

Notes on differentiation we discussed (to surface in comparison matrix):
- Smart routing + automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants keeps tails stable under load.
- Prefix/KV caching reduces repeated-context token cost for chat workflows — can show token cost delta in the test results.
- Transparent per-token billing + token-level trace in the Console aids debugging high-cost tails quickly.

I've attached a small CSV with the sample payloads we'll run and a one-page test plan. Happy to adjust if Acme needs different input lengths.

Cheers,
Marcus
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-v-hyperscalers-latency-sample.csv]
